methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native represent grassroots knowledge distribution outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for peer-based capability building in a military-economy region historically disconnected from NoVA's AI ecosystem.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education beyond NoVA, suggesting Richmond could develop as a secondary hub that bridges the capital region with underserved areas through community-focused training.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab directly addresses workforce readiness in Virginia's western region, demonstrating how smaller institutions can build deep AI fluency in areas facing economic transition from traditional industries.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: Residents questioning who benefits from the AI boom in the data center capital reveals that physical infrastructure concentration does not guarantee distributed economic or capability gains, potentially deepening rather than bridging regional divides.

signals.title: New Jersey, Virginia Can Lead the Nation By Building ‘AI Resilience Cohorts’ to Develop Early-Career, State Talent Pipelines - Federation of American Scientists
signals.signal_reading: Proposed AI Resilience Cohorts could institutionalize state-level talent pipelines, but success depends on whether programs genuinely distribute capability across regions or reinforce existing concentration in metro areas with established tech sectors.
